summary:
Desktop hostile QA of release/R1c/dist (9feb2ee6) against legacy/dist, 1440x900 primary plus 1280x720, 1920x1080, 2560x1440. Method: system Chrome 153, real CDP Input mouse/wheel/keyboard, each tree served by a static server on 127.0.0.1 (8500 R1c, 8501 legacy), Mapbox only via the Referer-injecting harness (every process stayed <=300 tile requests; three runs hit the cap exactly; total not summed, roughly 60 processes). Scripts and ~440 screenshots are in tmp/verify-desktop/ (git-ignored). Nothing outside that dir was written; legacy/ md5 7ef75b95... verified unchanged; git status clean.

Scale: ~140 checks run identically on both trees at 1440x900 (final consolidated batch: tmp/verify-desktop/logs2, matrix via aggregate.mjs), plus the viewport sweeps. Every fix claimed for desktop was proven RED on legacy and GREEN on R1c: real drag/wheel/zoom-buttons/right-drag/minimap (legacy 0 events, overlay canvas pointer-events:auto), Esc (pinned unit, Distance, search input, Layers), Ctrl+F/Ctrl+=/Ctrl+B inert, Space after clicking Play toggles once, C5 (legacy 'setGoldUnit is not defined' + 'kt.flyTo is not a function' page errors; R1c none), date +2 (legacy HUD prints July 3/4/5 at ticks 1/226/451; R1c July 1/2/3 and HUD==toolbar), day jumps load data (R1c 260/421 units at ticks 226/451, legacy ~72), idle React commits 0/s (legacy 60-74/s), 1 Document on first visit (legacy 2), no toolbar overlap at 1440 (legacy Virtual Walkthrough covers Search/Filter), Locations layer present, Help without heatmap/'445+', no sound control (legacy 'Enable cannon sound'), AR hidden+noindex, Watch Together HTML note not interpreted, Immersive Pause suspends AudioContext (running/suspended/running), dashboard/turning-points fixes, all deep links (tick/t/day/unit/u/ancestor/vignette/z/ll and Copy Link round-trip; 14 junk URLs degrade cleanly), keyboard-only Tab order starts at 'Skip to the map', blocked localStorage boots, full 1->675 play-through at 8x (0 errors, heap 12->14 MB), day boundary dates correct.

Console: R1c has 0 first-party errors in every journey except the Virtual Walkthrough, where Google Maps' own script logs 'Permissions policy violation: accelerometer is not allowed' (third party; also in legacy). With real headers (my header-applying server built from _headers) R1c additionally logs 'deviceorientation events are blocked by permissions policy' there, caused by Permissions-Policy accelerometer=(). Legacy: 12x the accelerometer message plus 3x 'kt.flyTo is not a function' and 1x 'setGoldUnit is not defined'.

Regressions vs legacy found (worked there, broken in R1c): (1) keyboard focus capture, (2) monument stars no longer track the map now that it can move. Details in defects. Pre-existing defects that R1c still ships are listed separately so they are not mistaken for regressions.

NOT verified / limits: headed run was still CDP-synthesised input (no physical mouse); no iOS/WebKit/Firefox/Samsung/real devices; Chrome 153 only; static-server runs except one header-applying pass (Netlify's real _headers/_redirects parsing, enforced CSP, netlify.app redirect, embed framing from a foreign origin not exercised); Lighthouse/RUM not run; sub-page Record (cinematic-export) and AR camera deliberately not pressed; Google Street View/YouTube content only checked as links; audio is muted (--mute-audio), only AudioContext state was asserted; legacy PAGE-* (menu click-through) rows are not a clean baseline because the legacy menu flow cascades failures; screenshots reviewed by eye for ~35 key states only at 1440/1280/2560, not all 440.

summary:
VERDICT: PASS WITH DEFECTS for the R1c phone shell. NOT TESTED: iOS Safari/WebKit, any real device, Firefox, Samsung Internet. Everything below ran in headless Chrome 153 on Windows with CDP touch emulation (Input.dispatchTouchEvent), SwiftShader GL and emulated safe-area insets. That means no real OS gestures, kinetic scroll, URL-bar/dvh behaviour, virtual keyboard, pull-to-refresh or notch hardware.

WHAT I TESTED: a byte-identical snapshot of release/R1c/dist (`diff -rq` clean; entry md5 198fc691...; legacy pinned md5 7ef75b95... intact; git status clean). I edited only tmp/verify-mobile/ and built nothing. I ran it at 320x568, 375x812, 390x844, 412x915, 768x1024, 812x375, 844x390 and 915x412, and compared against legacy/dist in the same harness. Scripts, JSON results and about 150 screenshots are in tmp/verify-mobile/ (git-ignored, so nothing to commit). I looked at about 40 of the screenshots, including onboarding, base, tools, story/event/unit cards, landscape states, tour, Help and Bookmarks. No browser or server of mine is left running.

RESULT, R1c mobile core: all 8 viewports pass.
- Layout: data-layout=mobile on first visit at all 8 (768x1024 gets the stretched phone shell, as chapter 14.14 predicts). One Document request, no chooser, no range input.
- One map: one style request and one sku with real tiles at 375, 320, 812x375, 768 and 915x412.
- Touch: drag, pinch, double-tap, blocked rotation and an unscrolled, unzoomed page pass at all 8 viewports.
- Controls: transport, day tabs (portrait), scrubber, all 14 Tools tiles, 21 Extra Features links (real taps navigate), Walkthrough (2 maps while open, 1 after Back), Bookmarks, Layers and Follow Ancestor work.
- Errors: 0 first-party pageerror or console.error. The only console error was a Google-embed Permissions-policy message from the Walkthrough Street View iframe, which is third-party.

LEGACY IN THE SAME HARNESS (regressions vs legacy: none found on the phone shell; R1c is a large improvement):
- Legacy makes 2 Document requests on first visit and shows "Choose Your Experience" about 5.3-5.9 s after load on every load and every new tab.
- After "Select Mobile" legacy builds 2 maps (2 skus, 4-6 style requests).
- Legacy map drag moves 0 m and pinch does not zoom (a z-10 canvas with pointer-events:auto sits on top).
- Legacy transport buttons are occluded by a desktop range input, and legacy has 31-47 small targets, 45 texts under 12 px and a "Invalid LngLat (NaN,NaN)" pageerror.
- Sub-pages: R1c fixed the horizontal overflow on compare (528 to 375 px) and dashboard (446 to 375 px). Everything else on sub-pages is unchanged from legacy.

SUB-PAGES AT 375 (24 pages): FAIL on the 44 px target and 12 px font criteria, and on overflow for sandbox only. All pages return 200 with 0 errors. 8 of 8 map pages render a non-blank map at 375 and at 320 (pixel std 41-80). All are pre-existing, not regressions, and the T0 plan does not claim to fix them.

PROCESS DEVIATION TO DISCLOSE: my first Google block covered only maps.googleapis.com and maps.gstatic.com, not www.google.com. In the first t2 and t3 runs (8 + 8 viewport sessions, before I widened it) the Virtual Walkthrough tile therefore loaded its Google Maps Embed Street View iframe (the app's own request, made from 127.0.0.1). I widened the block to all google, gstatic, googleapis and nps.gov hosts before the t3b, t7 and debug runs. A dedicated probe then showed 1 attempted request, failed with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT. The t7 run, which did not open the Walkthrough, logged 0 Google requests. I have not reproduced the key here.

MAPBOX TILE USAGE: Referer injection through the lib harness only. Every process stayed under the 300 cap (largest 248). Roughly 3,400 tile requests in total over about 30 processes, because I ran many viewports in parallel. Most network-only checks (t1, t8) ran with tiles blocked.

NOT VERIFIED: real touch feel and latency, iOS dvh/env(safe-area) on hardware (insets were only CDP-emulated), keyboard resize on a phone (I only shrank the viewport), Firefox, WebKit, Samsung Internet, Lighthouse. For the same reason, the landscape Tools sheet spilling into the right inset (D-08) is only emulation-backed.

Legacy: 2 Documents and chooser at ~5.3-5.9 s at all 8.

Privacy/Terms) each navigated by real tap to the right page (200, 0 horizontal overflow at 375). Ask the Historian navigates; Desktop View works (see D-01).

Numbers are equal or worse-by-measurement-artifact vs legacy (compare/dashboard overflow fixed).

Same harness, legacy/dist: chooser every load (~5.6 s), 2 Documents on first visit, 2 sku/2 maps after choosing mobile, map drag 0 m and pinch 0, transport buttons OCCLUDED by a desktop range input, 31-47 target-size issues and 45 <12 px texts in the mobile base, pageerror Invalid LngLat (NaN,NaN). summary:
Independent a11y + perf audit of release R0/R1a/R1b/R1c vs legacy/dist. Nothing outside tmp/verify-a11y-perf/ was edited; legacy/ (md5 7ef75b95... OK) and release/*/dist (every file hash matches its manifest) are untouched; git status clean. Tools: Chrome 153.0.8010.54 (headless=new, SwiftShader), Lighthouse 13.5.0 (installed only in tmp/verify-a11y-perf), axe-core 4.13.0, t0 harness lib for Referer injection; own brotli static server (tools/t0/serve.mjs serves identity only). Snapshots of the five dists are in tmp/verify-a11y-perf/trees; raw results are in tmp/verify-a11y-perf/out (lh/*.json, axe-*.json, kbd-*.json, contrast-*.json, probe/*.json, sw-audit.json, transfer-*.json, lh-tables.md).

ACCESSIBILITY. R1c `/`: axe 0 serious/critical in 14 desktop states, 6 phone states (375x812) and both first-visit states; Lighthouse a11y 100 (mobile+desktop, 5/5 runs; legacy/R0/R1a 90). Progression: legacy 3 serious/critical per state (color-contrast, label, scrollable-region-focusable), R0/R1a 3-4 (+target-size; R1a Layers panel 8 unlabeled inputs), R1b/R1c 0. Sub-pages (25 real pages + the GSC stub): legacy 23 of 27 pages have serious/critical; R1c still has 4 real pages at 1440 (cinematic-export, find-ancestor, embed, sandbox) and 5 at 375 (+privacy); X10 is therefore not met on the sub-pages. Keyboard-only on R1c: skip link, 55-stop tab order with visible indicators and names, map arrow-key pan/zoom, named slider (+1 tick per ArrowRight), Space play/pause, Help dialog open/close all work; FAIL: Help has no focus containment (Tab leaves after 3 stops, no aria-modal) and no search result can be selected by keyboard (0 of 3 routes). Legacy/R0/R1a layout chooser cannot be operated by keyboard at all. Important caveat: axe reports 48-144 color-contrast nodes per state as incomplete, so its 0 is not contrast evidence; I added an independent pixel-sampling contrast audit (text made transparent, background pixels measured): R1c body text passes (min median 4.77:1) but placeholder text (#757575) is 3.7-4.3:1 on the home search/ancestor inputs and 4.03:1 on 5 sub-pages, and sandbox helper text is 3.43/4.15:1. Two pixel-audit flags (education day tab 1:1, dashboard axis label 1.22:1) were checked by screenshot/computed style and are false positives.

PERFORMANCE (Lighthouse 13.5, real Mapbox tiles with production Referer via the harness, simulate throttling, median of 5; legacy -> R0 -> R1a -> R1b -> R1c). Mobile score 64 -> 84 -> 86 -> 89 -> 90; desktop 85 -> 100 for all trains. Mobile FCP 3939 -> 948 -> 947 -> 1090 -> 1091 ms; LCP 8882 -> 1301 -> 1289 -> 1419 -> 1451 ms; CLS 0.095 -> 0.050 -> 0.050 -> 0.000 -> 0.000; TBT 0 (artifact of the reload) -> 647 -> 553 -> 440 -> 420 ms; TTI 8897 -> 1960 -> 1834 -> 1970 -> 1970 ms; requests 143 -> 84 -> 86 -> 103 -> 103. Headline: R0 misses the runbook's >=85 mobile ship gate (84; runs 84/83/83/86/84; applied-throttling run 73) and its TBT (647 ms) is above the chapter's 190-470 ms prediction; R1a-R1c pass 85 and only R1c reaches 90. With tiles blocked R0 scores 99, so the plan's replica numbers are tile-free upper bounds (real tiles cost ~15 points via TBT). Document requests on first visit: legacy 2, every train 1 (LH 5/5 runs, browser net log, server ledger). Service worker: controller set 0.75-1.1 s after load with no navigation in all trains; upgrade drill legacy->R0/R1a/R1b/R1c passes (1 Document, old entry never requested, 0 exceptions, Help and Bookmarks open, new worker waits, gbg-v5 purged after all tabs close); kill drill leaves 0 registrations and only mapbox-tiles; rollback R0->legacy restores the reload band-aid (2 Documents, 0 exceptions). Reload-fix-alone claim: NOT reproduced under default simulated throttling (62 vs 64, range 54-64; +8 with tiles blocked) but reproduced under applied throttling (46 vs 66; LCP 6.0 s -> 15.0 s, FCP 1.1 -> 5.2 s). Combined R0 recovers it (84 simulated, 73 applied). The intro deletion is invisible to simulated Lighthouse (84 vs 84) but decisive when throttling is applied (LCP 15.7 s -> 1.5 s; 4x CPU probe 10.3 s -> 0.57 s), which confirms the plan's LCP-element diagnosis. First-visit bytes as served (brotli, tiles blocked): legacy 94 requests / 1420 KB (bundle downloaded twice, 2 x 549 KB), R0 47 / 709 KB, R1c 47 / 715 KB (phone 50 / 734 KB). Camera sub-page mobile 75 -> 100 (plan expected ~86).

SIMULATED vs OBSERVED. Lighthouse's own observed (unthrottled, final navigation) FCP/LCP: legacy 217/4617 ms, R0 121/121 ms, versus simulated legacy 3939/8882 and R0 948/1301. Legacy's simulated FCP includes the discarded first document; in a 4x-CPU, 1.6 Mbps probe the first legacy document never reached first-contentful-paint before the SW reload at ~3.4 s. Legacy's TBT of 0 and the redirects penalty (610 ms mobile, 180 ms desktop, not the plan's 9,066 ms) are artifacts of that reload.

WHAT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED. Real iOS/Android devices, Safari/WebKit, Firefox, Samsung Internet; any screen reader (NVDA/VoiceOver/TalkBack) or voice control; real Netlify headers/compression/CDN latency (own server emulates them) and production RUM; real-mouse check on the live site; contrast of text drawn directly over real map imagery; 30-day field data. The host was shared with other agents (Lighthouse-run CPU busy median ~30%, range 20-41%; Lighthouse benchmarkIndex ~4200) and headless SwiftShader replaces a real GPU, so absolute TBT and scores are environment-specific; relative deltas between trains were measured in interleaved runs. Mapbox use: ~120 separate harness processes, each under the 300-request cap (max 73), roughly 4,000 Referer-injected requests in total, all through lib.openSession.

Builds are deterministic, references resolve, asset names are never reused, legacy/ is untouched, the drills pass, and the 36 suites re-ran green. They are NOT safe to deploy yet because of one high-severity finding. Production no longer equals the legacy/dist baseline. Live data/terrain.json and live index.html differ from legacy/dist, and neither live version exists in any of the 127 archived zips. Every train is built from the stale baseline, so any deploy would silently revert those two live files (defect 1). The runbook also has factual errors and untested steps.

What I did, all inside tmp/verify-release:
- **Rebuild:** cloned HEAD 8a004d0 and ran build.py --all from scratch. All four dists are byte-identical to release/*/dist (my own hasher, 122/124/124/128 files). A second build into other directories, and a build with a different TZ, locale, hash seed and cwd, also matched. The only exception was --order runbook, where version.json and _ops/asset-manifest.json differ because they record the group order.
- **Independent checks:** my own reference crawler, strict /assets/ check, archive-zip name scan and eslint-scope check all agree with the builder's gates.
- **Drills and headers:** I wrote my own upgrade drill (seeded from legacy/dist plus the old gbg-v5 worker) and my own L2 kill drill (45 s watch for reload loops). I also ran an independent header/redirect analysis on _headers/_redirects and the ops/headers-probe emulator.
- **Diff accounting:** every shipped byte re-derives from legacy + patch JSON + overlay + R0 mechanism output. The one exception is R0's index.html and site-nav.css, where I compared the mechanism hunks to the plan by hand. The 54 changed, added or removed files in R1c are all classified; none is unexplained.
- **Suites:** I re-ran all 36 builder suites from the clean clone (R1c-tier 178/179 green + 1 skip, R1a/R1b 154/176 with 22 skipped by design, 9 red-first proofs RED as required), plus npm run t0:test, the build self-test, verify_release and the overlap audit. About 1,500 Mapbox tile requests in total, all through the harness, each run under its 300 cap.
- **Notes and docs:** all identity numbers in the four release notes verified, and the notes regenerate byte-identically from release_notes.py.

Could NOT verify:
- Real devices, iOS/WebKit, Firefox, Samsung Internet; a real mouse on the live site.
- Lighthouse gates (no runner exists).
- Netlify's own header and _headers/_redirects semantics, CLI vs drag-and-drop handling, staging deploy, rollback timing and credits.
- RUM; the runbook's section 7 deploy steps; the schtasks step (I did not touch scheduled tasks).
- sha384 SRI values recomputed from the CDN files (I corroborated them by size, ETag and jsDelivr's sha256 instead).
- npm ci (it would download packages).
- Runbook section 8 step 5 (git tag, ledger record, tools/commit.sh): the permission system blocked it and I did not retry.
